newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM SAYS FOUND NO CASES OF SWINE FEVER SO FAR.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM SAYS FOUND NO CASES OF SWINE FEVER SO FAR.

text.p: Belgium has found no cases of swine fever despite an intensive slaughter and testing campaign following outbreaks in Germany and the Netherlands, Agriculture Minister Karel Pinxten said on Wednesday.
"We have not found one case of swine fever in this country," he told a news conference.
Belgium banned all imports of pigs from Germany on February 1 and added a ban on imports from the Netherlands 11 days later.
It has slaughtered and tested 15,142 pigs that were imported from the Netherlands between January 15 and February 12. All the carcases, which weighed a total of 510 tonnes, were destroyed.
Pinxten said the cost of the operation to date was 53 million francs, of which 10 million were operational costs and 43 million were compensation for the slaughtered animals.
He said the 56 businesses from which the pigs had been taken for slaughter had been quarantined until extra blood samples had been taken for a final check.
Vigilance could not be relaxed. "The development of swine fever in the Netherlands, Germany and also recently in Italy still constitutes a threat to the pig herd in Belgium," he said.
